entries.title: Architecture proposal and Project Blueprint v1.0
entries.request: Design the architecture first (AI videos, images, simulations, chemical reactions, teaching assistant) in Python; after approval, put the plan with workflow and IAD flowchart into Word documents in a docs folder.
what_i_did: Proposed the architecture: Streamlit UI, FastAPI later, LLM orchestrator with tools, Manim/RDKit/JS simulations, RAG on the syllabus, phased plan.

After the owner's answers (State Board content via uploads, teacher on laptop, English default with Hindi/Marathi on request, multi-provider and low cost, local first), wrote Blueprint v1.0 with 6 diagrams (architecture, teaching workflow, ingestion/RAG, model routing, lesson pipeline, roadmap).
Checked the laptop first (no Python, no FFmpeg, RTX 3050 4 GB, 32 GB RAM, Ollama already installed with some models) so the plan matched the real hardware.

files.change: Created (now in docs/archive/)
Created 6 diagrams

issues.problem: All arrowheads in the diagrams pointed sideways.
issues.cause: The SVG renderer (resvg) does not support orient="auto-start-reverse" on markers.
issues.fix: Used orient="auto" with a separately drawn reversed marker for double arrows.

issues.problem: A label overlapped a box in the teaching-workflow diagram.
issues.cause: Loop arrow placed too close to the box.
issues.fix: Moved the loop line further right and widened the canvas.

commands: Word COM export to PDF to visually check every page
lessons: Always render and look at generated documents/diagrams instead of assuming they are right.

entries.title: LiteLLM supply-chain safety rules → Blueprint v1.1
entries.request: After the March 2026 LiteLLM incident: pin versions, use lockfiles with hashes, isolate API keys, filter network egress.
what_i_did: Verified the incident (LiteLLM 1.82.7 and 1.82.8 on PyPI were malicious; 1.83.0+ clean).
Added Section 14 to the blueprint: SDK only (no proxy server), exact pins, SHA-256 lockfile, 7-day release cooldown, keys in Windows Credential Manager, in-app host allow-list.
Explained honestly where the guidelines needed adapting for a single laptop (Credential Manager instead of a cloud vault; firewall rules only once deployed).

files.change: Created (now in docs/archive/)

lessons: A security rule must be translated to the actual setup (laptop vs server) — and the adaptation written down for approval.

entries.title: Phase 0 — secure foundation, AI gateway, cost control
entries.request: Start building; be accurate; write a short README with all steps; keep docs updated.
what_i_did: Installed FFmpeg 9.0.2 and MiKTeX 25.12 (winget verified installer hashes); Python 3.12.14 via uv.
Created the project with exact version pins and a hash-locked uv.lock; pip-audit clean.
Built the task-based LLM router: fallbacks, retry, monthly budget cap, premium approval, host allow-list, response cache, cost log.
Startup security checks (pinned clean LiteLLM, malicious .pth file, keys not in .env, localhost binding, keyring backend).
Streamlit shell (bound to 127.0.0.1, usage statistics off), 48 offline tests, README, Blueprint v1.2.

files.change: Exact pins; exclude-newer cooldown
settings, secrets (keyring), logging with key redaction, startup checks
router, LiteLLM backend (only LiteLLM import), config, health
Home + pages
48 tests

issues.problem: Ollama model 'qwen3:4b' spent 190 tokens 'thinking' before a one-line answer (15–25 s) and ignored think=false.
issues.cause: That tag is Qwen3-4B-Thinking-2507, a thinking-only model.
issues.fix: Switched to 'qwen3:4b-instruct' (answers directly, ~22 tokens/s).

issues.problem: LiteLLM downloads its price list and a headers file from GitHub every time it is imported.
issues.cause: Library default.
issues.fix: Set LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True and LITELLM_LOCAL_ANTHROPIC_BETA_HEADERS=True before import; a test blocks all sockets and proves zero connections.
issues.type: Library behaviour (found by reading its source)

issues.problem: A pricing-page summary listed a model 'gpt-6-luna' that does not exist.
issues.cause: The web page was summarised by a small model that made an error.
issues.fix: Used only models confirmed by two sources (pricing page + LiteLLM price list) and added verify_models to check availability with the real key.

issues.problem: Tests failed: 'Datetime values must have timezone information'.
issues.cause: SQLModel 0.0.47 requires timezone-aware datetimes; I used naive UTC.
issues.fix: Switched all timestamps to timezone-aware UTC.

issues.problem: Pages crashed with 'No module named common' when opened on their own.
issues.cause: They only worked because the Home page had added the ui/ folder to Python's path.
issues.fix: Each page adds its own folder to the path; the UI test now removes it before each page.

issues.problem: I tried to commit to Git; the owner rejected it.
issues.cause: I had not asked first.
issues.fix: Standing rule: never commit; the owner commits.

code.why: Stop LiteLLM from contacting GitHub at start-up (only the model endpoints we choose may be contacted).

lessons: Measure models on the real machine — tags with the same name can be very different models.
Read a library's source when it matters for security.

entries.title: Pushing to GitHub (guidance only)
entries.request: Explain the steps to push the codebase to github.com/31skpandit/AI_Tutor_Simulation_App; the owner pushes manually.
what_i_did: Checked read-only that all_key.key and .env are git-ignored and not staged.
Gave step-by-step commands; recommended a private repo, GitHub push protection, and moving keys out of all_key.key into Credential Manager.

entries.title: Phase 1 — textbook ingestion, review, search, AI tutor
entries.request: Upload PDFs (or images/docs) from Streamlit or the source folder, process automatically, never re-ingest duplicates; add all testing/teaching steps to the README.
what_i_did: Built ingestion for PDF / images / DOCX / TXT with 3-level de-duplication (file SHA-256, page-image SHA-256, passage text hash).
Resumable background jobs, Review Text page, SQLite + NumPy vector search (instead of ChromaDB: avoids ~30 heavy packages), tutor with page citations and Hindi/Marathi on request.
Ran the owner's 17-page scanned chapter end-to-end; calibrated the 'not in textbook' threshold on real questions.

files.change: files, extract, ocr, chunking, service, CLI
vector store and grounded tutor
background worker
new/rewritten pages

issues.problem: The PDF had no text layer at all (0 words on every page).
issues.cause: It was 'printed to PDF' as images.
issues.fix: Every page goes through OCR with a vision model.

issues.problem: OCR took 90–178 s per page.
issues.cause: 'qwen3-vl:4b' is again a Thinking model; the 4b-instruct model does not fit in 4 GB VRAM; Ollama's default context (4,096) was too small.
issues.fix: Benchmarked on the real page → 'qwen3-vl:2b-instruct' at 1600 px with num_ctx 8192: ~27 s/page, same text.

issues.problem: Page 16: OCR wrote one line 196 times and lost the rest of the page.
issues.cause: Small vision models can get stuck in a repetition loop.
issues.fix: Detect loops (compression ratio / repeated lines) and retry once with repeat_penalty 1.1; otherwise remove repeats and flag the page ⚠️.

issues.problem: File names with underscores (std10_maths_chapter-3) were not recognised.
issues.cause: In regular expressions '_' counts as part of a word, so word boundaries failed.
issues.fix: Normalise _ - . to spaces before matching.

issues.problem: The Devanagari examples in tutor.py became garbage characters.
issues.cause: I edited the file with PowerShell 5.1 Get-Content/Set-Content, which reads ANSI and writes a BOM.
issues.fix: Rewrote the file in UTF-8, scanned all files, added a test, and stopped using those commands for project files.

issues.problem: The tutor added its own analogy and a stray 'not covered' sentence.
issues.cause: Small model not following instructions strictly.
issues.fix: Stricter rules in the prompt and automatic removal of the stray sentence.

issues.problem: 'Review pages' link crashed when the page was opened on its own.
issues.cause: st.page_link needs the multi-page registry from Home.py.
issues.fix: Button + st.switch_page with a specific error fallback; UI test with a real document added.

code.why: Detect a stuck OCR output: normal pages compress to ~44 % of their size, the stuck page to 7 %.

lessons: Benchmark on the owner's real pages before choosing a model.
Never edit UTF-8 files with Windows PowerShell 5.1 text cmdlets.

entries.title: Phase 1 improvements — tables, cloud re-read, summaries, answer reuse (Blueprint v1.4)
entries.request: Tables and images were read badly; owner proposed Unstructured/LangChain + Redis. After discussing, owner asked to implement the proposed alternative: table preview, cloud re-read, summaries, similar-question cache.
what_i_did: Benchmarked local vs gpt-5-nano vs gpt-5.4-mini on pages 3, 4, 5, 16 → gpt-5.4-mini for optional cloud re-read (~$0.005/page).
Review preview tab and lossless Markdown table repair; page summaries/table/figure descriptions; answer-model switch; semantic answer cache with calibrated threshold.
Re-indexed the owner's reviewed chapter (88 search entries).

files.change: table repair, cloud re-read, summaries
answer cache, originals-only evidence, index change counter
adds new columns to existing databases

issues.problem: I said page 5 had the table; it was page 4.
issues.cause: I assumed page numbers instead of checking.
issues.fix: Checked the page image, re-ran the benchmark on page 4.

issues.problem: My cost estimate for gpt-5.4-mini was $0.002/page; measured $0.005.
issues.cause: Estimated instead of measured.
issues.fix: Used the measured value everywhere.

issues.problem: My table repair deleted blank exercise rows.
issues.cause: An empty row matched my 'separator row' rule (all() of nothing is True).
issues.fix: A separator now needs at least one non-empty '---' cell.
issues.type: Claude bug (caught by checking real output)

issues.problem: A generated table description swapped 'acidity' and 'basicity'; the tutor repeated it.
issues.cause: Small-model descriptions can be wrong, and I first let them be used as evidence.
issues.fix: Descriptions only help find the page; the tutor receives original passages only.
issues.type: Claude design mistake (caught by live test)

issues.problem: After re-indexing a page, search could keep using the old vectors.
issues.cause: SQLite reuses row ids, so my 'count + max id' change detector did not change.
issues.fix: A real change counter (IndexState.generation).

issues.problem: 'Suggested for cloud' listed all 17 pages.
issues.cause: Almost every page has a figure.
issues.fix: Suggest pages with tables or warnings; 'all pages' is a separate button.

code.why: Generated descriptions FIND pages; only ORIGINAL textbook passages are given to the answering model.
An all-empty table row is not a separator row (bug fix).

lessons: Generated text is a search aid, not a source of truth.
Never trust 'count + max id' as a change detector in SQLite.

entries.title: Learning log started + Phase 2 — lessons, equation checker, 3D molecules, safe simulations, Teach Mode (Blueprint v1.5)
entries.request: Use the 3 suggested pilot topics for Phase 2. From now on record every code change, issue, fix, command and suggestion in docs/Claude Interactions.docx so the owner can learn from the mistakes and see how the AI thinks.
what_i_did: Created this learning log: data in docs/_source/interactions.json, Word file generated by gen_interactions.js (npm run interactions); back-filled the earlier sessions honestly.

Added RDKit 2026.3.6 (pinned) and stored p5.js 2.3.3 and 3Dmol.js 2.5.5 inside the project (npm --ignore-scripts, lockfile integrity, SHA-256 manifest checked before every use) so lessons work offline.

Wrote an in-house equation checker (atoms + charge, hydrates, ions, electrons) instead of chempy; molecule table + RDKit 2D/3D; lesson planner from original passages with page citations and one automatic equation-correction round.
AI-written p5.js simulations with safety rules, structure checks, `node --check` syntax check and up to 2 automatic fixes; shown in a separate frame whose security policy blocks all network access.

Lesson Studio (create / edit / regenerate / approve) and Teach Mode (slides). Generated the 3 pilot lessons from Chapter 5 (~$0.06 total) and reviewed their content and simulation code against the textbook.
160 automated tests, pip-audit clean, README section 3c, Blueprint v1.5.

issues.problem: Two of the three pilot lesson jobs failed with 'Unknown job kind lesson_plan'.
issues.cause: The owner's app had been running since before Phase 2; its background worker (old code) picked up the new jobs first and failed them.
issues.fix: Workers now only claim job kinds they support (others stay queued). Lessons 2 and 3 were generated directly; README tells to restart the app after updates.
issues.type: Process / version mismatch (found in the live run)

issues.problem: New lesson tests failed: 'No reviewed textbook pages match'.
issues.cause: The fake word-count embeddings used in tests score lower than the real model, so the real 0.45 threshold filtered everything out.
issues.fix: Threshold became a setting (default 0.45 for real use); tests use 0.1.

issues.problem: My first charge-parsing code tried to guess whether 'Fe3+' means a 3+ charge or three Fe atoms.
issues.cause: Over-engineering an ambiguous notation.
issues.fix: Simplified: charges must be written Fe³⁺ / Fe^3+ or a single sign (OH-); ambiguous ASCII is reported, never guessed (tested).

issues.problem: The rule against accessing the surrounding app would also have rejected harmless code like box.top.x.
issues.cause: Pattern too broad ('top.').
issues.fix: Narrowed to the dangerous forms (window.parent, top.document, …) and added a test with harmless look-alikes.

issues.problem: Lesson 3 listed ferrous sulphate, washing soda and alum, which were missing from the molecule table ('not available').
issues.cause: The local table only covered the substances I expected.
issues.fix: Added the three substances and a test that every molecule used by the pilot lessons is available.
issues.type: Claude mistake (caught by reviewing the generated lessons)

issues.problem: I wrote a pointless helper function in viewers.py just to keep an unused import.
issues.cause: Sloppy code.
issues.fix: Removed both.

issues.problem: An edit to the molecule-name list did not apply.
issues.cause: The code formatter had re-wrapped the block, so the text I searched for no longer existed.
issues.fix: Re-read the current file and applied the edit again; verified by test.

issues.problem: The session was interrupted by an 'API Error … safeguards flagged this message'.
issues.cause: The AI service's automatic safety filter occasionally flags normal technical conversations (false positive); not caused by the project or the owner.
issues.fix: Nothing was lost (all work is on disk); the work was resumed in the next message.

code.why: The app — not the AI — decides whether an equation is balanced: atoms of every element and the total charge must match on both sides.
Every AI-written simulation must pass all checks; problems are sent back to the model to fix (at most 2 times).
The page that shows a simulation is not allowed to contact the internet at all (Content-Security-Policy).
code.snippet:
CSP = (
    "default-src 'none'; script-src 'unsafe-inline'; style-src 'unsafe-inline'; "
    "img-src data: blob:; font-src data:; connect-src 'none'; worker-src blob:"
)

code.why: Fix for the live incident: a worker never takes a job type it does not understand.

commands: cd docs/_source && npm run blueprint && npm run interactions
lessons: After changing code, restart every running copy of the app — old processes keep old code.
Let deterministic code check AI output (equations, code safety) instead of trusting the AI.
Review generated lessons yourself: the review found missing molecules that no automatic check flagged.
